findings.evidence: `extEuler_eq_inverseCartanMatrix` (line 169) takes `hend : ∀ i, Module.finrank k (Module.End A (S i).obj) = 1`. Counterexample to the docstring as written: `k = ℝ`, `A = ℂ` (semisimple, so all resolutions are finite), one simple `S = ℂ`, `C = (1)`, but `E = χ(ℂ,ℂ) = dim_ℝ End_ℂ(ℂ) = 2 ≠ 1`.
findings.fix: Add the hypothesis: "...and every simple is absolutely simple, then `E i j` is the `(j, i)` entry of `C⁻¹`".
findings.issue: Overclaim: "If `A` is finite-dimensional and every finitely generated module has a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives, all these pairs are Euler-admissible and `E i j` is the `(j, i)` entry of `C⁻¹`" omits the absolutely-simple hypothesis. Without it only `Cᵀ * E = diagonal (dim_k D i)` holds.

findings.evidence: Line 171: `(hend : ∀ i, Module.finrank k (Module.End A (S i).obj) = 1)` is a hypothesis of the theorem; the theorem's own docstring (line 166) does say "absolutely simple".
findings.fix: State it as "for absolutely simple simples under finite projective resolutions, ...", matching the bullet for `transpose_cartanMatrix_mul_extEuler` on line 45.
findings.issue: Same omission in the Main results list: "`TauCeti.extEuler_eq_inverseCartanMatrix`: under finite projective resolutions, `χ(S i, S j)` is the `(j, i)` entry of the inverse Cartan matrix" — the absolutely-simple hypothesis is missing here too.

summary: The module docstring of ExtEulerMatrix.lean states the identity `E = (C⁻¹)ᵀ` under only finite-dimensionality and finite projective resolutions, dropping the absolutely-simple hypothesis that the theorem actually requires; the same omission recurs in the Main results bullet. The PR description also misdescribes its own diff.
